assumes: 'Nice is in Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur' gives way: Nice still lies in one administrative region, which the kept premises and the edit make Liguria, in Italy (the County of Nice belonged to the Kingdom of Sardinia before 1860).

worlds.summary: The Promenade stays in Nice, so Nice alone belongs to Liguria; the rest of the region stays French.

notes: Derived edit (0015, added for relation-property coverage, CRITERIA Rule 12) with derived-belief queries. Derivability very_likely: the Promenade's region is almost never written down (84 co-occurrences in about 59,000 mentions, none stating it; 11 'Promenade des Anglais is in' in all), while the Promenade being in Nice and Nice being in Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur are each stated often. The new region was chosen across a national border so that the transitivity query discriminates: Liguria is in Italy, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur in France, and the bridge 'Liguria is in Italy' is political, so it holds in both worlds (a physical container such as a continent would not have discriminated). Worlds: the Promenade's city gives way (w1), or Nice's region does (w2); the 'located in' rule is definitional. w2 has history behind it (Nice was Savoyard until 1860), and it moves Nice alone, so Monaco's neighbours and the rest of the region stay French; Nice becomes an Italian exclave, which contradicts no firm fact outside the chain. The French Riviera route (the Promenade is on the Riviera, which is in the region) goes with the Promenade in w1 and with Nice in w2, as the worlds say. The premise-route query reaches the edit through 'the city the Promenade runs along' (binding), not by restating it. Near query: Lyon's region (Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes), not the new answer and not a premise. R2: the Promenade's names (英国人散步大道, Paseo de los Ingleses) name no region. Prompts say 'administrative region' because 'Côte d'Azur' is also loosely called a region. Since 2026-10-31 (formal check, FINDINGS E and C3) the worlds name only the premise that gives way, with the side facts, and the one-region and one-country presuppositions are bridges.
